changes.headline: January WCS traded 895 lots wider to end the strip's four-session tightening run, while December marked tighter for a fourth straight session on zero lots
changes.dek: TMW Jan27 -$24.40 (-$1.05, 895 lots vs 620 tightening lots Monday); Dec26 -$28.49 (+$0.41, 0 lots, fourth straight zero-lot tightening); Feb27 -$22.95 (250 lots); Mar27 -$21.95 (250 lots); ARV Dec26 -$18.98 (0 lots); ARV Jan27 -$17.00 on 1 lot. ARV to TMW: December +$9.52, January +$7.40. December WCS outright $57.55 on Tuesday's WTI settle of $86.04.. The Nov 10 ICE file reverses the strip's direction. January WCS is -$24.40 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 10), wider by $1.05 on 895 lots against 620 lots tightening it on Monday, and the widening ran the length of the traded strip: February on 250 lots, March on 250, and July through September on 225 lots each. December is -$28.49 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 10), marked tighter by $0.41 on zero lots, its fourth consecutive zero-lot tightening, so the front month's mark and the strip's traded direction point opposite ways. Houston widened in parallel, December at -$18.98 on zero lots and its traded volume deferred to April through September. December MSW is +$0.58, December SYN +$8.48, December C5 +$9.17 and December UHC +$4.75, each on zero lots (ICE settles, Nov 10).
changes.balance_read: The strip's November tightening was a traded trend until Tuesday; it now has its first traded counter-evidence, printed on the month's heaviest January volume, while flat price was stabilising rather than falling. December's mark no longer corroborates the strip because the strip itself has turned; a traded December settle, in either direction, is now the front month's missing fact.
changes.publishers: ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 10, 2026; ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 9, 2026

changes.headline: Tuesday settled at two-month lows with CTA length cut from 45 to 9 percent long, and the API printed a 9.0 million barrel crude build ahead of Thursday's delayed report
changes.dek: Tuesday settles: Brent Jan27 $91.49 (-$1.08, -1.2 percent, lowest since Aug 31), WTI Dec26 $86.04 (-$0.81, -0.9 percent), Brent to WTI spread $5.45 (from $5.72 Monday). Wednesday 0730 GMT: Brent $92.01 (+0.6 percent), WTI $86.20 (+0.2 percent). API w/e Nov 6: crude +9.0 Mbbl, distillate +1.5 Mbbl, gasoline flat, Cushing +0.182, SPR -2.7 to 279.5 on the API count. Diesel crack $89.08 validated.. Tuesday settled at two-month lows and Asia bounced: Brent Jan27 settled at $91.49, down 1.2 percent, and WTI Dec26 at $86.04, down 0.9 percent (Reuters, Nov 11; Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 10), after an intraday break below $90 in Brent that recovered part of the loss. Trend-following CTA length in Brent was cut to 9 percent long on Tuesday from 45 percent at Monday's end (Kpler via Bloomberg), and physical barrel premiums are falling. The API bulletin for the week ending Nov 6 printed a crude build of 9.0 million barrels and a distillate build of 1.5 million barrels (Reuters market sources), against a calendar consensus near a 1.0 million barrel crude draw; a conflicting draw print circulates in calendar feeds and is not carried. The EIA's November outlook has Brent averaging $99 in December and $86 in 2027 as inventories rebuild.
changes.balance_read: Flat price is now falling in smaller steps with a mechanical positioning leg identified, and the balance evidence has its first loosening print in the API week. None of it is confirmed until Thursday: the EIA print grades the API, the consensus, and every narrative built on them, and the distillate line decides whether the products leg of the tight case survives the week.
changes.publishers: Reuters, Nov 10-11, 2026; Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 10, 2026; API via Reuters market sources, Nov 10, 2026; EIA STEO, Nov 10, 2026

changes.headline: A tanker was hit off Limah and an ADNOC vessel was damaged in UAE waters on Tuesday, while Ukraine struck the Ust-Luga export terminal overnight and Abu Dhabi sat for a second day
changes.dek: UKMTO Warning 201-26, 13:38 UTC Nov 10: tanker hit by unknown projectile 19 NM NE of Limah, crew safe. ADNOC vessel damaged in UAE waters Nov 10, extent unpublished, relationship to the Limah report unestablished. AIS-visible crossings: 4 on Nov 10 (0 tankers), 3 by 09:02 UTC Nov 11 (1 tanker), 7-day average 6.9 a day (floor gauge). Ust-Luga strike overnight Nov 10-11: fire, 3 injured, power station offline; terminal handles roughly 700 kb/d. Kirishi confirmed hit Nov 9 (fire, one fatality in the region).. Tuesday added fresh incidents inside the blockade: UKMTO Warning 201-26 reports a tanker hit by an unknown projectile northeast of Limah, Oman, crew safe, and ADNOC confirmed one of its vessels damaged in UAE territorial waters the same afternoon; no authority has established whether they are one incident or two, and Iran's Guards' mine claims for the day are unnamed and unverified. AIS-visible crossings were 4 on Nov 10, none tankers, a 7-day average of 6.9 a day, carried as a visibility floor; Gulf crude exports are separately estimated at 80 to 85 percent of pre-war including pipeline volumes with products at 35 to 40 percent (ING, Nov 10). Ukraine struck the Ust-Luga export terminal overnight (fire, three injured, power station offline) and the Kirishi refinery hit is confirmed; Abu Dhabi's second day runs with no outcome and an unanswered energy-truce offer.
changes.balance_read: The corridor's crude is moving at a rate the visible count cannot measure, through bypasses and dark channels, while its products remain constrained and its incident rate is rising during the diplomacy. The export-terminal strike extends the refinery campaign's target set to Russia's Baltic outlet, which is a products and export-availability fact regardless of how Abu Dhabi closes.
changes.publishers: UKMTO, Nov 10, 2026; ADNOC Logistics and Services via WAM, Nov 10, 2026; Reuters, Nov 10-11, 2026; ING, Nov 10, 2026

flags.title: December apportionment: the registered call is Light 14 and Heavy 9, the balance shows about 200 kb/d a month looking for tank space, and nominations close Nov 17
flags.detail: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect from Nov 1. The registered December judgment call is Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent. The evidence pack now includes the balance build with November and December supply running about 192 and 216 kb/d above the proven 4,541.6 kb/d egress bound into tanks, a January differential that has printed the first traded widening of the month on 895 lots, a December front month that has marked tighter four straight sessions without trading, and a Brent to WTI spread at $5.45 keeping the export leg shut. December nominations close Tuesday Nov 17; the Enbridge notice follows the close and grades the call. Trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment notice in mid November, or a material change in the November physical backdrop before the nominations close

flags.title: Distillate stocks at their lowest since May 2003 meet the API's first build print: Thursday's release grades both
flags.detail: Distillate stocks are 99.3 million barrels, the lowest since May 2003, after a 3.565 million barrel draw in the week ending Oct 30. The API bulletin for the week ending Nov 6 printed a distillate build of 1.5 million barrels and a crude build of 9.0 million, the first loosening signal against the stocks position, with a conflicting draw print circulating in calendar feeds. The validated diesel crack is $89.08, up from $86.94. Russian refining capacity is estimated down about 30 percent since late October, tightening the same products pool from the other side. The next inventory report is Thursday Nov 12; the weekly balance forecast lands ahead of it. Trigger: The EIA release at 12:00 p.m. ET on Nov 12, a distillate stock build back above 105 million barrels, or a diesel crack break in either direction

flags.title: Price is falling on unsigned rhetoric while the flow gauges conflict in kind: the snap-back test stays live
flags.detail: Brent has fallen for three straight sessions to its lowest settle since Aug 31 on de-escalation rhetoric, with no agreement signed, the blockade kept, and incident reports rising inside the strait. The flow gauges conflict in kind: AIS-visible crossings run at 6.9 a day, about 8 percent of the normal visible rate, while Gulf crude exports are estimated at 80 to 85 percent of pre-war including pipeline volumes and products at 35 to 40 percent. Trend-following length in Brent was cut from 45 percent long to 9 percent long in a day, so part of the fall is mechanical. Factors on the board are listed; no single driver is established, and the configuration is the one the causal discipline exists for. Trigger: A signed instrument or a measured flow recovery through the strait, a confirmed corridor incident with assessed damage, or the Thursday Nov 12 inventory print

forward_calendar.what: US-hosted Ukraine and Russia talks, Abu Dhabi, Day 2 (Nov 10-11); OPEC monthly report due
forward_calendar.detail: Day 2 of the first trilateral round since Geneva on Feb 18. Day 1 produced no closing statement or ceasefire; a prisoner exchange of 1,000 to 1,500 per side was discussed and is officially unconfirmed, Russia has rejected a ceasefire first, and Kyiv's offered truce at sea and on energy targets is unanswered. The OPEC monthly report is also due today and had not been published at edition time.

forward_calendar.what: EIA weekly petroleum report, 12:00 p.m. ET (delayed for Veterans Day)
forward_calendar.detail: The inventory report for the week ending Nov 6 is released a day late for Veterans Day. The API printed a 9.0 million barrel crude build and a 1.5 million barrel distillate build; distillate stocks at 99.3 million barrels, the lowest since May 2003, are the line that matters.

The deadline for December shipper nominations. The registered December judgment call (Light 14 percent, Heavy 9 percent) grades against the Enbridge notice that follows the close, with the balance showing roughly 200 kb/d a month looking for tank space into the notice.

forward_calendar.detail: The wider group meets to set the 2027 production framework, with the fourth quarter capacity review setting the baselines for 2027 quotas.
